Summary
This letter, dated July 23, 1945, is a heartfelt communication from a parent to their son Jack, expressing concern for his well-being and providing updates on family matters. The sender, Beckerman, mentions receiving Jack's letter and is glad to hear from him. They express worry about Jack's living conditions and inquire about his food and possessions. The letter also discusses Jack's pictures, a check of $1300 sent to the bank, and the sender's hope for Jack's return home in good health. The tone is warm and caring, with the sender expressing a desire to see Jack soon and mentioning other family members like Abe and Ruth. The letter concludes with the sender's busy schedule and their love for Jack.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_39a) --- July 23, 1945 Dear Son Jack! The last days we received your letter of July 13. We are more than glad to hear from you. We feel the harsh in your daily life now. To live in a hunt [illegible] place. Did you get at last your proper food? We like to know are you are not all your things? Now son! one of your picture the one with a half of your clothes We had a lot pleasure to look at you, you look very beautiful. We are looking forward for the pictures you took with Abe. Now Jack I wrote you in my last letter that I received your check of $1300 and on the second day I went to the bank and I gave the check with your bank book to the manager and he made out the deposit. With such a big sum I do not want to go now to the post office to send it to you. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_39b) --- Two thousand dollars my wish is I should see you soon home in good health and make your life hope with a good girl... Jack! I don't know Ola! is not coming up to us for the last few weeks. I guess she is busy with [illegible]... did you get any mail from her? Well everything at home is the same papa told this summer letter than last because it is not so hot and you could see I am a little busy with writing letters to you and Abe and Ruth. I am glad with myself although I know it is not a perfect English but I fell a mother is easy to understand I know Abe will it is now good but I can help... Yes Jack you probably got some letters from Ruth. I get from her 4 or 5 letters every week I sent all yours and Abe's letters I will finish up who are destas me. I'll whove you a [illegible] for a closeth to me. The [illegible] loving mother and [illegible]
